claims.claim: There are three first-party adapters (Omnia, AgentCore, Vertex)
Omnia substrate is an Omnia Kubernetes workspace
AgentCore substrate is AWS Bedrock AgentCore
Vertex substrate is Google Agent Runtime
Omnia deploys CRDs in a workspace
AgentCore deploys runtimes plus supporting resources
Vertex deploys one engine per agent
Maturity: Omnia most complete, AgentCore feature-rich/older, Vertex newest/narrowest
get_provider_info is implemented by all three
validate_config is implemented by all three
plan is implemented by all three
apply is implemented by all three
destroy: Omnia Yes, AgentCore Yes, Vertex No
status: Omnia Yes, AgentCore Yes, Vertex No
import is not supported by any of the three
All three reject import with an error saying it is unsupported
Vertex is the only adapter where tearing down a deployment is a manual step
Agent runtime resource type is agent_runtime on all three
Omnia packs are deployed as a prompt_pack CRD
AgentCore injects the pack as env
Vertex injects the pack as env, or stages a pack_object in GCS when over the inline limit
Omnia tools become a tool_registry CRD
AgentCore tools become tool_gateway (MCP targets)
Vertex tools are injected as env (PROMPTPACK_TOOL_SPECS)
Omnia policy is an agent_policy CRD
AgentCore policy is cedar_policy
Vertex has no policy resource
Omnia memory is config on the runtime
AgentCore memory is a memory resource
Vertex has no memory resource
Omnia evals are config on the runtime
AgentCore evals create evaluator and online_eval_config resources
Vertex evals run in-process from the pack
Omnia A2A is handled via the platform
AgentCore A2A is an a2a_endpoint resource
Vertex has no A2A
Omnia and AgentCore model capabilities as platform resources; Vertex ships everything inside the container as environment
All three adapters read the arena's tool_specs
Omnia runs tools on the platform via a tool_registry CRD
AgentCore runs tools on the platform via tool_gateway targets
Vertex runs tools in the agent's own container
Omnia does not dispatch on the spec's mode
AgentCore does not dispatch on the spec's mode
Vertex dispatches on the spec's mode
Omnia supports HTTP with full request/response mapping
AgentCore HTTP transports: HTTP, Lambda ARN, API Gateway, OpenAPI, Smithy
Vertex HTTP supports url and method only
Omnia additional handler types: openapi, grpc, mcp, client via its own tools: block
AgentCore MCP is supported via the gateway
Vertex has no additional handler types
Omnia credential support: headers from env, static headers, redaction
AgentCore credential providers: GATEWAY_IAM_ROLE, OAUTH, API_KEY
Vertex has no credential providers
Omnia does not forward mock_result / mock_template
AgentCore does not forward mock_result / mock_template
Vertex forwards mock_result / mock_template
Only Vertex runs mock tools; the AgentCore runtime has no mock handling
Vertex is the only target that reproduces promptarena run behaviour for mocked tools
Only Omnia and AgentCore authenticate live tools
Vertex forwards URL and method and nothing else (no headers, timeouts, redaction, mapping)
If tool_specs never reaches the adapter, tools are advertised with nothing to run them, on every target
Omnia unary request/response is supported
AgentCore unary is POST /invocations
Vertex unary is POST /api/reasoning_engine
Omnia server-streamed output is platform-dependent (unverified)
AgentCore streams SSE on /invocations
Vertex streams ndjson on /api/stream_reasoning_engine
Omnia persistent bidirectional socket is unverified
AgentCore persistent socket is a GET /ws upgrade carrying text messages
Vertex has no persistent bidirectional socket
Omnia server-side sessions are provided via the platform
AgentCore sessions use the X-Amzn-Bedrock-AgentCore-Runtime-Session-Id header
Vertex does not use server-side sessions in the adapter
No target does duplex voice (AgentCore and Vertex)
No target does duplex voice (Omnia)
AgentCore /ws upgrades, holds the connection, and processWSMessage unmarshals a text request with prompt/input and writes one response
No adapter runtime calls PromptKit's OpenDuplex()
sdk.OpenDuplex() exists alongside Open()
Conversation has SendChunk, SendFrame, SendVideoChunk
PromptKit duplex includes VAD and barge-in handling
For Vertex the reasoningEngines REST surface has query, streamQuery, asyncQuery and no bidirectional method in v1beta1
Whether AWS/Google control planes proxy a WebSocket upgrade to a custom container is unverified
Only AgentCore carries multi-turn context for you
Vertex opens a fresh PromptKit conversation per request and holds no state between calls
Agent Runtime exposes a sessions API but the adapter does not use it
Omnia observability config surface is cluster-provided
AgentCore config surface is observability.tracing_enabled
Vertex config surface is observability.tracing_enabled + otlp_endpoint
AgentCore traces go to CloudWatch
Vertex traces go to any OTLP collector
AgentCore metrics are CloudWatch metrics from evals
Vertex emits no metrics
AgentCore eval scores in telemetry via online_eval_config
Vertex eval scores appear as gen_ai.evaluation.score spans
Vertex guardrail firings are logged only, never traced (PromptKit guardrail hook adapter emits no event)
Declaring an evals section produces scores in telemetry
Omnia adapter authenticates to the control plane with OMNIA_API_TOKEN
AgentCore adapter uses AWS credentials
Vertex adapter uses Application Default Credentials
Omnia agent authenticates to model provider via Provider CRD reference
AgentCore agent uses AWS IAM for models (Bedrock)
Vertex agent uses ADC as the engine's service account
Omnia API keys in config are avoidable via the env var
AgentCore and Vertex have no API keys in config
Each target deploys one deployment per agent
Omnia routes between agents via the platform
AgentCore routes between agents through a2a_endpoint wiring
Vertex has no routing between agents
A multi-agent Vertex pack becomes independent engines that cannot call each other
Vertex agent cards are generated but cannot be attached
spec.agentCard exists in v1beta1 REST discovery doc, is absent from published protobufs, so the Go client has no field
Omnia has the richest tool handler support and full lifecycle
AgentCore provides memory, Cedar policies, A2A wiring, session continuity as managed resources
Vertex gives Gemini models with the least moving parts
Choose Vertex if you accept that teardown is manual
Choose Vertex if you accept there is no A2A
With Vertex live tools cannot authenticate
Vertex is the pick if your pack depends on mocked tools
None of the targets do duplex voice today
